title: Horace Henderson's Stompers and the press roll
summary: Describing the Horace Henderson band's name, book, personnel with Jonah Jones and Matthew Harlan, and his dislike of press rolls.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So Horace... That was the Horace Henderson Collegians? Was that the name of the band?
Were they at Wilberforce at that time?
Well, that was after that band. I don't know whether he called them The Fletcher Henderson Stompers under the direction of Horace Henderson...
I think that's what they were called. And Fletcher Henderson was Orchestra, period, you know; these were the Stompers.
Did you play Fletcher's book? Or was it a different book?
No, I think it was Horace's book. We had some of the things of Fletcher's, but not the things like when I got with the band and I played. Nothing like that, you know.
And that was a full-sized band with what? Three trumpets...

Oh yeah, yeah. See, Jonah Jones was in the band. Jonah Jones and a good trumpet player, I guess he's dead now, Matthew Harlan. You ever hear of him? Boy, that cat could swing, man. He was from Louisville, too. Myself. In fact, I can't remember nobody else in that band... That's

funny. I can't remember nobody else in that band. But there was a cat that played baritone from Indianapolis; I vaguely remember him. And Van Sherrill, who was an alto player. He was very good. I forget who was on bass. And then there was a cat who was on drums named Bill something; because I used to pay him a quarter to play the top cymbal for me, you know, because I wanted to get away from that press roll.
Oh yeah? You already felt like that then?

Oh, I always did, yeah. I like the press roll on certain things, but most of the cats tend to overdo it, you know. Shadin' it, like Zutty used to say. I said, "Well, you dropped that (?)." "I was shadin' Pops." Heh-heh. But I'll you one thing. Zutty used to march on that "Chinatown" we used to play. Maybe he had something, you know. Really!
